title: Collector Dimitris Daskalopoulos Donates 51 Works to Greek and Scottish Museums

title: After Many Delays, Kanal-Centre Pompidou in Brussels Will Open in November
summary: The Kanal-Centre Pompidou, acollaboration between the Centre Pompidou and the Brussels-based institution Kanal, will finally open on November 28 after a decade of planning, renovations, and delays. title: 2026 Winners of $50,000 Rabkin Prize Announced
summary: The Dorothea and Leo Rabkin Foundation on September 10 named the eight recipients of its 2026 Rabkin Prize for arts journalists. Each will receive an unrestricted grant of $50,000. Established in 2017, the honor recognizes the contributions of journalists writing about the visual arts for a general audience and has distributed $4.1 million since its inception. title: Gerhard Richter–Designed Pavilion Celebrating the Artist to Rise in Doha
summary: Qatar Museums has announced that Doha will welcome a permanent pavilion devoted to Gerhard Richter this autumn. The building will occupy the city’s MIA Park, outside the Museum of Islamic Art. title: Louisville’s Speed Art Museum Names New Director
summary: Kathleen V. Jameson has been named the new director of the Speed Art Museum, in Louisville, Kentucky. She officially began her role on Tuesday. Jameson specializes in late-nineteenth- and early-twentieth-century American art, with additional expertise in photograph and works on paper. title: Tschabalala Self Unveils Fourth Plinth Sculpture in London
summary: American artist Tschabalala Self has unveiled Lady in Blue (2026) on the Fourth Plinth in London’s Trafalgar Square. Her sculpture, cast in bronze and patinated with lapis lazuli blue—a pigment used in in north Africa, the Middle East, and Europe since antiquity—will remain in place for two years. title: Freelands Foundation Announces £100,000 Annually for Three UK Arts Organizations
summary: The Freelands Foundation has awarded £100,000 (approximately $135,000) of unrestricted funding to three organizations annually for the next five years, totaling £1.5m (roughly $2 million). summary: The Amon Carter Museum of American Art in Fort Worth has announced Robert Stein as its new executive director and CEO. summary: Historian Lonnie G. Bunch III, who has served as secretary of the Smithsonian since 2019, has announced that he is leaving the institution.
